913767.title: The printed count sheet follows the Total Qty sort order
913767.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create three tracked parts for this test: part A with one bin location holding 5, part C with one bin location holding 3, and part B with two bin locations, one holding 5 and one holding -3 (below zero), so part B's Total Qty cell shows 5 Available while its bins add up to 2.
  • Give parts A, B and C descriptions that start with the same text and end, in turn, with ALPHA, BRAVO and CHARLIE.
  • Give parts A, B and C part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists all three.
  • Make sure no Cycle count is running on the Inventory list.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
913767.custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the Total Qty column header.
  3. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  4. Click Cycle count.
  5. Click the printer icon in the count toolbar.
  6. Close the print preview without printing.
  7. Click Cancel in the count toolbar.
913767.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A, B and C are listed.

Step 2:

  • The Total Qty header shows a sort arrow.
  • Low to high, the rows read part C (3), part A (5), part B (5). High to low they read part A (5), part B (5), part C (3). One of these two orders shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu opens.

Step 4:

  • The count starts with parts A, B and C on screen.

Step 5:

  • The count sheet lists parts A, B and C in the same order as the list: part C, part A, part B from low to high, or part A, part B, part C from high to low.
  • Part B's two bin rows sit together, where part B sits in the list: it is placed by its shown 5, not by 2, its bins added together.

Step 6:

  • The print preview closes.

Step 7:

  • Cycle count ends and the three-dot actions button is back in the toolbar.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 36 (3 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10819 (Story 6, Search and Sort the Inventory List by Tracking State), story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List)

  • S6-R5: “Tracked parts sort against each other by the quantity shown in the Total Qty column. The printed count sheet follows the same order.”
  • S6-R3: “The Total Qty column can be sorted.”
  • S6-R6: “Tracked parts with the same quantity are then ordered by description, A to Z.”
  • S1-R10: “Cycle count is offered on both tabs. It counts the parts on the tab that shows, and the printed count sheet lists those parts.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 18: “"5 Available." The Inventory list counts only bins above zero, the same as production today, and this feature doesn't change it.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "5.7 Cycle count leaves it out". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

913768.title: Delete stays disabled while a work order line received the entry's part
913768.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a Part Library entry for this test, entry A, with no part behind it: create a part at the test location, then delete it, so the entry stays with "Total parts" 0.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with a line, line 1, holding entry A's part added by picking its "Part Library" result, then ordered from any vendor and received onto line 1, so line 1 received it and no inventory part uses entry A.
  • Start on the Part Library page (Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu).
913768.custom_steps:
1. Type entry A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the entry A row.
  3. Click the pencil icon beside the entry's name in the Part details panel.
  4. Hover over the Delete button at the bottom left of the window.
  5. Click the Delete button.
  6. Click Cancel.
913768.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Entry A is listed.

Step 2:

  • The entry's detail page opens and shows "Total parts" 0: no inventory part uses it.

Step 3:

  • The "Edit Library Part" window opens.
  • A Delete button sits at the bottom left of the window, dimmed (disabled): line 1 of work order 1 received the entry's part.

Step 4:

  • Hovering it shows "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first."

Step 5:

  • Nothing happens: no "Are you sure you want to delete this library part?" question opens and the window stays open.

Step 6:

  • The window closes and entry A is still there.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 36 (3 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only)

  • S11-R3c: “While an inventory part, an open part request, a work order line that received it, or a part return (open or credited) still uses the entry, the Delete button is disabled and hovering it shows "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first."”
  • S11-R3: “Clicking a row opens that entry's detail page. The pencil beside the entry's name opens the "Edit Library Part" window, where the entry is edited and where its Delete button sits, bottom left. The detail page itself has no Delete button.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Delete on a Part Library entry a part still uses | "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first." | Hover text on the disabled Delete button (S11-R3c)”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 14 Oct 2026, answer 12: “Board 7.2 is right: the page has no Delete button. Delete sits bottom left in the "Edit Library Part" window, opened by the pencil beside the entry's name (S11-R3). While a part uses the entry, Delete is disabled with the hover text "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first." (S11-R3c).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "7.2 An entry opens its detail page". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

The board 7.2 note quoted below says the entry "can be edited and deleted" on its page. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 20) that this note is out of date: the detail page has no Delete, and Delete is in the "Edit Library Part" window. The expected results follow the PRD.

The design's own words:

  • “Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3). New entries come only from a part number in use (S11-R6).”

913770.title: A part request picked from the Part Library result takes the new number
913770.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with 5 on hand.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with a line holding two part requests, neither ordered nor received: one added by picking part A's "Part Library" result, and one where part A's number was typed by hand and added as typed, with no link to the part.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
913770.custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Work Orders in the top bar.
  6. Open work order 1.
  7. Click the Parts tab.
  8. Click Order on the row of the part request picked from the Part Library result.
  9. Click Parts in the top bar.
  10. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  11. Open the newest purchase order.
913770.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved, the window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 5:

  • The Work Orders list opens.

Step 6:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 7:

  • The part request picked from the Part Library result reads the new number: it is linked to part A.
  • The part request typed by hand still reads the old number: it only shares the number and has no link to part A.

Step 8:

  • The part request is ordered and goes through.

Step 9:

  • The Parts left menu shows Purchase Orders.

Step 10:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 11:

  • The new purchase order's line reads the new number, not the old one.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 36 (3 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19a: “A line that only shares the old number, typed in by hand with no link to this part, keeps its number. A part request added by picking this part's Part Library result is linked to it, and takes the new number.”
  • S13-R19: “A rename carries over to open work that holds this part, at every location: purchase order lines not yet fully received, part requests not yet received or returned, canned jobs, and returns that are not completed take the new number. A delivery that is not yet accepted is covered by its open purchase order lines. Receiving, ordering, applying a canned job and returning then find the renamed part.”
  • Terminology: “Open work → A purchase order line not yet fully received, a part request not yet received or returned, a canned job, and a return that is not completed.”

913771.title: A received vendor bill line refuses an inactive part's typed number
913771.custom_preconds:
BLOCKED ON RELEASE: this test checks SV-12010 (Vendor bill: refuse an inactive part's number on a received line), which is not released yet. Do not run it now. It can be tested once SV-12010 is released.

Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part for this test, part A, with a hyphen in its part number, and set it inactive.
  • Create a received vendor bill for this test, bill A, with one special-order line, line 1, whose part number was typed by hand and matches no part at the test location.
  • Start on bill A (Parts in the top bar, Vendor Invoices in the left menu, then bill A).
913771.custom_steps:
1. Click line 1's part number to change it.
  2. Replace line 1's part number with part A's part number in lower case.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Replace the text with part A's part number with periods in place of its hyphens.
  5. Click Save.
  6. Reload the page.
913771.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Line 1's part number can be changed.

Step 2:

  • The field holds part A's number in lower case.

Step 3:

  • The save is refused with a message: part A's part number, written as it was saved (capitals and hyphens), followed by "is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it."
  • Line 1 keeps its own typed number.

Step 4:

  • The field holds part A's number with periods.

Step 5:

  • The save is refused again with the same message, part A's part number followed by "is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it.": upper and lower case and periods make no difference.

Step 6:

  • Bill A reloads and line 1 still shows its own typed number: neither change was saved.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 36 (3 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S9-R17: “The system refuses an inactive part on new work however it arrives: adding a part to a work order or estimate line, raising a part request or special order, adding a part sale line, and adding a purchase order line or changing its part or number. The refusal reads "{part number} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it."”

From: Jira SV-12010 "Vendor bill: refuse an inactive part's number on a received line" (Task, Board Backlog, requested by Chris Ward in SV-10647 comment 79703; saved word for word in sources/jira-2026-11-04/SV-12010-2026-11-04.md), read 4 Nov 2026

  • SV-12010, Expected: “The save is refused with "{part number} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it.", as S9-R17 does for purchase order lines.”
  • SV-12010, Expected: “Same match as S9-R17: upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored; a number an active part at this location also has is not refused.”
